utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I received it when I came to The Hague, Your Honour. Actually, a day after I arrived. But it was here in The Hague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Now did you receive it before you were interviewed by the attorneys or was it at the first interview? And what was told to you when this bundle was given to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When I arrived at the Hague, the following day I had a talk with the lawyers and that's when I received this document. They told me that was my statement, that there was some maps there, that I would need to read it. But I asked them, What does this mean, because it's in English. And the lawyer said that it's a map as if it wasn't really that important in relation to me. I asked because I don't know what it says in English, and he explained that it's a map of sorts which is not really something that applies to me, so I didn't really pay much attention to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, once you had been given this and when you were invited to read it all, were you then interviewed later again? Or was that the last time you saw the lawyer before you came to this courtroom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I got the document, I read it. And during the talk with the lawyer, then I took it to the room with me and I read it, I took it with me so that I could refresh my memory before the trial. We just had that one conversation before the trial. That's when I got the document. It was this proofing preparation. Of course, I took the document. And my statement is there just so that I could refresh my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you had not received it before this meeting with the lawyer. You received it when you met with the lawyer. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now the striking of the Metalka. You told us that there was a line stricken through there. Was that there already or did you raise the matter during that -- at that occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes. I said that Metalka had nothing to do with me, and I underlined that portion, and I told the counsel that. He said that that would be corrected, that it just was inserted there by error. He did not know himself how it happened to be there, and that's how it went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now, apparently you read your statement at that occasion. Now, did you read during that meeting all of the other materials in that bundle as well, or did you just read your statement when you met with the lawyer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, I read the statement. They also showed me a couple of maps. And I looked at that, too, and said about this thing and that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But it was not given to you before you met with them. It was during that meeting that you read the materials and that you went through those maps. Is that correctly understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Before -- I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just find out. You say you received this statement in Budva. When the person who sent the statement to you sent it to you, where had he got the information on the statement from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I'm not sure I understood this well. This person was probably a member of the Defence team. He had received information before that because I met the attorneys in Sarajevo in 2013 and that was the statement at hand. I just didn't sign it then. I don't know why I didn't. But I actually frequently went to Montenegro, and when they came to Sarajevo I wasn't there so I didn't have an opportunity to see them before.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I don't follow you. Now, your last sentence you say you didn't have an opportunity to see them before but you then say that you were in Sarajevo before in 2013. I'm not quite sure what you are saying. Surely before this document was composed, was written out, the person who wrote it must have received this information that you put in there. Where did he get it from? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I really don't know. What I'm saying is in 2013 we met - I met - the attorneys two or three times and that's when I made my statement. Now, later on in May 2014, they sent this for signing because at the time I was in Budva. I wasn't in Sarajevo. Had I been in Sarajevo, I would have signed it there probably because they did come to Sarajevo and that's why I signed it in this manner.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, when you were in Sarajevo and when you made the statement, what did you tell them about the contents of the statement?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time I did not sign the statement in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Stop, stop.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As I said, what I was saying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just stop there. I'm not asking you about your signature. I'm asking you what did you tell the lawyer in Sarajevo about the contents of the statement that he then later put on paper and sent to you to sign. What did you tell them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am not following.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yeah, in Sarajevo when you met them in 2013. You say you met them three times. What did you tell them about the contents of this statement which they later then wrote down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, again, I don't follow you. When I was in Budva, I called. After sending the statement I called them up on the phone. I had a number from which this attorney would call me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- but he wasn't there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. We don't seem to know. You say at page 47, lines 9 to 16: "Your Honour, I am not sure I understood this well. This person was probably a member of the Defence team. He had received information before that because I met the attorneys in Sarajevo in 2013 and that was the statement at hand. I just didn't sign it then. I don't know why I didn't, but I actually frequently went to Montenegro. And when they came to Sarajevo, I wasn't there so I didn't have an opportunity to see them before." Now, you say he received information before that because "I met the attorneys in Sarajevo in 2013." I'm asking you: When you met them in 2013 in Sarajevo, what did you tell them about the content of that statement? Because as I understand you, after you told them what you told them, they went and wrote the statement. You went to Budva. They then sent the statement to you by e-mail recording what you told them for you to sign. Is that how it within the?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And I want to know what is it you told them about the content of this document in Sarajevo in 2013.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, when I provided my statement they were taking notes. And later, when we finished this interview, they said that we would meet again and that's why I didn't sign the statement there in Sarajevo. They said we will have to meet again, if there is anything you want to add, and so on and so forth. However, when they called me later on, I was in Budva. And then I read the statement and I noticed this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- reference to Metalka and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: When you were talking to them in Sarajevo, did you say -- talk about Metalka building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't think so. Maybe they asked, but I probably said I didn't know anything about that because that wasn't in my zone of responsibility. It was in another area. Now, I don't know where this confusion came from. We never discussed Metalka.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you talk --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We didn't talk about it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you talk about anything related to something called F4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Do you mean at the time when I talked with the attorneys?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers]

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] They did -- yes, I believe that was the incident we -- we are discussing here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they told me there was this incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What is F4?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that's the incident relating to the positions below our positions that we cannot really see, that a woman and a child were killed there, if that's what you mean. And that the Prosecution thought that this was by fire from our positions, but I didn't see that. So I think that's the incident in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I ask you one question in addition to the question that Judge Moloto has put to you. When you were interviewed, was the starting point open new questions or did you start looking at your Karadzic statement and then to go through that? I'm talking about the interviews you had on the three dates in 2013.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, there was the Karadzic statement. I had it. I read it. And we just added a couple of things. In the Karadzic statement, the same incident was mentioned in that same statement because I also -- I talked with the Prosecutor, whether it was Christopher or someone else, about this particular incident. I think there was another incident. I think number 10 or something and we discussed that then. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Practicably there were these two incidents as far as my positions were concerned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore, I understand you well that during these interviews the starting point was your Karadzic statement which you went through and then added or changed to the extent you considered it appropriate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, for the main part that's how it went.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see it's time for a break. Or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm making a mistake. Mr. Shin, you're on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I don't think we have further questions from the Bench at this moment. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could please have a screen shot of the document on the ELMO and the Prosecution would tender that into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. You mean the handwriting?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Exactly as it's imaged right now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Can we have a screen shot from what is now on the ELMO, Madam Registrar. Madam Registrar needs to consult first with the technicians. Another way of dealing with it is to -- Mr. Shin, another way of dealing with it is to make a copy of your copy --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- show it to the Defence and see whether it really is what we looked at at this moment and then upload that into e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, I -- I think that perhaps that's the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Most practical way.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- more practical way of doing it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Usher, please, could you assist Mr. Shin in showing to Mr. Stojanovic what he intends to upload into e-court and then ask whether there is any objection to that to be admitted. Yes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then, Madam Registrar, could you already reserve a number for the document still to be uploaded?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The reserved number would be P6623, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is reserved for a English chart with some handwriting on it among which the date of the 27th of 06, that is June, 1992. Please proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. And if Mr. Usher could kindly assist me with one more reference in this bundle. It's ten pages from the back -- or ten pages from the end. I recognise that that's double-sided. So it would be the tenth page from the end of the bundle and the ERN in the upper right-hand corner ends in a 3043. It's a typed list of names, not the handwritten one. My -- thank you, Mr. Usher. If we could just look at the left side of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, you see that under the names number 5, Petar Svalina, and number 11, Himzo Sulejmanovic, there is underlining. Whose underlining is that, Mr. Tusevljak?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I underlined that because these were my fighters of Croatian and Muslim ethnicity.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. No further questions on that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And I won't need that document further, Mr. Usher. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then it can be returned to the witness. Mr. Usher, you can return the document to the witness, but the witness should keep it closed and not consult it until having received permission to do so. Please proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, we're going to go back to your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If I could please have D539 on the screen again. Just one question on this.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If you -- the page that we have right now, this says "Witness Acknowledgement." You read this before signing the document; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. Well, we have that text. I won't ask you anything further about it. Now, I'm going to go to -- you were just talking about a few minutes ago about something about the 4th Company and the 2nd Battalion.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Let's turn to paragraph 2 of this document, that would be on the second page of both the English and the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now in paragraph 2, you state that you were in: "The 1st Company in which I was platoon commander of the 1st Battalion." Now, both the company number and the battalion number here is simply incorrect; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right. And I mentioned this a little earlier to the Trial Chamber when I talked about Metalka, that that was an error. There was -- I also mentioned that there was an error of sorts here, because it was the 4th Company -- the 4th Battalion -- 2nd Battalion, 4th Company. So whoever wrote this down made an error. I made a mention to this, to the attorneys, the numbers of the battalion and company were incorrectly written down.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. First of all -- whoever wrote it down. But you're the person who signed this document, this one-and-a-half-page document, you reviewed and you signed it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, sir. But I've already told you how this happened. Had I been in Sarajevo, I would have probably corrected it right then and there and then signed it. But because I was in Budva, I was in no position to correct it, and I thought it could be done here.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, here in court during your testimony you, along with the rest of us, have heard no correction of this designation of the 1st Company and 1st Battalion, and yet you've said nothing; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I believe this was something we talked yesterday, I believe. I told the attorney -- my attorney that this was incorrect, both this and the Metalka thing. I think we already talked about this yesterday, that this should be corrected.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Well, we didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now I'm going to move to paragraph 8.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One more question. You said you couldn't correct it. Well, if you sign with your own pen, you can make small correction on numbers as well, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could have done that but the attorney wasn't there so I just sent it as it was. And then I thought that before I start testifying that could be done, corrected, and changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But you could have done it in Budva?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I could have. But I've already described it was quick.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] And just to be clear --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just to be clear, Mr. Tusevljak, the company number and the battalion number, those are material differences, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't know if they are material differences. But it is well known that this was not the 1st Battalion. It was the 3rd Battalion first, and then 2nd; and the company, the 1st Company was below us towards Grbavica. We were the 4th Company and to the left of us was the 5th Company. Now, I don't know why this is so important, whether it was the 1st or 4th, it's the same battalion. Now how this error occurred, I don't really know.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I think it's obvious --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, I have to interrupt again. Mr. Tusevljak, at the beginning of this paragraph 2, it says, "In paragraph 7 of the said statement," the said statement is the statement D540 of the Karadzic case. When you read this document in Budva, did you compare it with the statement given in the Karadzic case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, because I didn't have that. I didn't have that with me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This I can very well understand. In paragraph 7 of the Karadzic statement, nothing is written about battalions and brigades. That is in paragraph 13 of the Karadzic statement. There are similar mistakes as well, the references to the Karadzic statement. I just wanted to put that on the record. Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Now I think it's time for the break, Mr. Shin.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was a bit early. But, Witness, we'd like to see you back in 20 minutes from now. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We resume at 25 minutes to 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second, please, Mr. Shin. I'm just dealing with another matter for a second. Mr. Shin, you wanted to raise a matter before the witness comes in.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Actually, I think it's fine even if the witness comes in. But just in the interest of time, two points: One, the document -- the screen shot document -- well, what we had wanted to get a screen shot of is now in e-court under 65 ter 30922. And I understand it is -- it was, of course, already signed a P number. And --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: 30922. And Your Honour is correct, I sped up on the numbers again. Second matter, we have noticed that in the bundle of documents that the witness has, there is at lease one confidential document. It's a confidential. It's -- of course, it was disclosed. It's fine for use by the Defence. But it would be inappropriate to let the witness take it away from the premises, we believe, so we would request that the witness be instructed to return that document to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And perhaps the Defence should give an explanation for that situation. If you have one second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, we don't have access to the bundle. So if we want to ask the witness something, then at least you should guide us what document to -- for the witness to return to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. It may be safest for the entire bundle to be returned to the Defence --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- after the witness's testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And possibly even at the end of session today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: At the end of session today.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that's the appropriate way. And, Mr. Stojanovic, the Defence owes an explanation to the Chamber for what Mr. Shin describes had happened; that is, that you leave a confidential document with an outsider. But could I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry, it's no a statement. I should be clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No, I --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's a document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's a document. Now, Witness, could I ask you: Were you instructed in any way how to deal with specific documents in that bundle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, Your Honour, I was just instructed to read my own statement, and basically that was it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Did you ask to keep them or were they just left with you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked to have them with me so that I can go through them in my hotel room and look at the maps and such-like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And you didn't receive any other instructions; for example, how to deal with maps or how to deal with your statement or that you did receive any specific instruction as how to handle each and every of those documents?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, for the most part I kept that in my bag. When I needed them, I would read them then and put them back in the bag, and basically that's how it was. I understood those to be personal documents that no one else should read them other than me, and that's how cared for them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But you didn't receive any instructions in that respect, did you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, no, nothing specific.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I mean, you could have shared your statement with your wife upon return, for example? I don't know whether you are married or not. But ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, yes, I am married. But, no, I mean, she is not interested in these things. So I just held onto them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand. Mr. Shin, we'll take appropriate measures at the end of this session. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, now, when we left off you were just telling us that you did not believe that company numbers and battalion numbers were material facts. I'll just leave that there and go on to another issue. But let me ask you just this: If -- you were a soldier, you were in the war for four years. It did make a big difference what the company of a unit was. That's a complete different unit, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, yes. But I know the unit I was in. I know what it was called. I know where it was, where I was, and so I -- I said as much that these numbers weren't correct. That this was an error. But I didn't see it as particularly significant to me. I'm not a lawyer. So I did mention to the lawyer that this should be corrected, that and the Metalka issue.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on now. But also staying with your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: If we could have the next page of what is D539. And that's on our screens now.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: While we're turning there, Mr. Tusevljak, I'm going to ask you to focus on paragraph 8. Now, in your statement you refer to a -- to a train and a mortar, and you say that it was running along Vasa Miskina Street, and you also refer to paragraph 12 of your Karadzic statement. Now, Vasa Miskina Street, this is also an error, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think so. That is Vasa Miskina Street. There was a rail track along that street and the train moved along those tracks. We received information from people who could see it from Sarajevo. They told us that there was this train that would fire the shells and then it would enter a feature, a building where it would be hidden. I think it was on Vasa Miskina street.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, let's turn to the document that's currently under D540. This is going to be your Karadzic statement, Mr. Tusevljak, and we will go to paragraph 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And -- I'm sorry, that's the next page, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, here you'll see --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We should have the B/C/S on the screen --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. If we could please have that back. Oh, yes. I don't believe there is a B/C/S version of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So I will read it to you. The second sentence reads: "In the attack, they fired mortars mounted on railway tracks in depth of our territory from the centre of the city near the Vaso Miskin Crni Enterprise." Now, here, Mr. Tusevljak, you're talking about the Vaso Miskin Crni Enterprise. That is a building near the Brotherhood and Unity Bridge, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, but I thought that street, too, was Vasa Miskina Street and I know exactly where this enterprise is. I think that it -- that the street, too, is called Vasa Miskina Street. That was my impression.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You've lived in Sarajevo all your life, you say. Vasa Miskina Street --

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Vasa Miskina Street, that's in Bascarsija, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Possibly. I didn't really remember street names particularly, but I guess because I mentioned the company, the enterprise, then perhaps I made a small error. But certainly it was from that place. We could see that part of the city from our positions, just that part where this enterprise was. And so I probably made an error with the street name but probably thinking about the enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We'll leave that and move on, but I'll just ask you: The location of the Vaso Miskin Crni Enterprise and the location of Vasa Miskin Street, those are two completely different parts of town. You'd agree with that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now we've reviewed some of the errors that were still in this -- some of the errors you've corrected and some of the errors that are still in this one-and-a-half-page statement, and I have to ask you: Are you sure you understand the importance of being truthful and accurate in presenting your evidence before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes. I do understand. But an error can slip in. For instance, this Vasa Miskin Enterprises and I said "street," but I know what I meant where this was because that's where the tracks were.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm going to move on to different topic, now. And what I would like to ask you about is the weapons that your platoon and your company had.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could I please have on the screen the document that is now D545.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Tusevljak, while we're waiting for this, you'll recognise this list as a list of people in the 1st Platoon. But let me ask you first: Your name does not appear on this list; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could you explain briefly why that might be?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this list was probably compiled after I moved to the other platoon. I was no longer a member of the 1st but of the 2nd Platoon. So that's probably why.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay. But you recognise the names here; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. Yes. These are all my neighbours and the fighters who were with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, we see a reference to an M-84 at numbers 9 and number 21. That's a heavy machine-gun, correct, one that fires a 7.76 millimetre cartridge?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You testified in the Karadzic case --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And that's transcript 29958.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You testified that you believed a target at 1200 metres would be within the M-84's effective range if it had optical sights. You stand by that; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Yes, it could reach that far.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now, we're looking at that -- these M-84s and we see a number next to them. In fact, we see numbers next to all of these weapons. That is the weapon's serial number; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And that is a unique number that is listed there so the company can keep track of weapons; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now let's look at -- a little further down at number 23, I believe, where it says PM-M 53. That is also a machine-gun; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's a machine-gun, an older model.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: At number 5, we see a reference to a Zbrojevka-Brno. You described that in your Karadzic testimony as a Czech-made weapon similar to a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: That's T29936 and -37.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: You stand by that testimony; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. It's similar to a machine-gun.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now we see an M-48 appearing twice at numbers 18 and 25. That is a rifle that was also known as a Tandzara; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: In addition to these weapons we've seen here, did your platoon have Zoljas?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we had several Zoljas and we had a hand-held launcher in order to be able to breach the fortifications ahead of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And you also had grenade launchers; correct?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was a hand-held grenade launcher. It was an impact-action launcher. It was meant for breaching trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, if you could just focus on my question. If I have a question about how a weapon or what a weapon is for, I'll ask that. Now, in paragraph 13 of your Karadzic statement, you state that your platoon had a 60-millimetre mortar; is that right?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: The company had that weapon, not the platoon. That's another error. There was a mortar in the company which was in the rear of our lines.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Let me ask you: Was there only one mortar of 60-millimetre calibre or were there more in your company?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe there were two. However, one of them was out of service. There was something wrong with it so it wasn't in use, a 60-millimetre mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: So when your statement in the Karadzic case --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: And again, this is paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: -- says, "We only had one 60-millimetre mortar," even accepting your clarification that that's for the company, that statement is incorrect?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as I've already said, the other one was out of order. So I know it wasn't in use. There were some men who had been issued with that mortar, but they said that it was out of order so it wasn't in use.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Mr. Tusevljak, were there three mortars of 60-millimetre calibre, one of which may have been out of order? Or were there two 60-millimetre mortars, one of which may have been out of order?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I am not sure. It wasn't really within my purview. It was something that the company commander would be responsible for and the supply officer. I know that one of them was out of order, but I don't know if there were actually three of them. It's possible, but I don't know. I was not responsible for mortars. I just knew that when there was an attack I would communicate with them and tell them to send the shells, and that was it.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We will look into this further, but, for now, let me focus on the latter part of your sentence in paragraph 13. That whole sentence reads: "We had" -- "We only had one 60-millimetre mortar but no mortar bombs." Now, we've already recognised the need to make a correction on the first point. The second point: When you say, "We had no mortar shells," is that the company you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's my company. And I believe I mentioned there that on that day, on the 8th, we didn't have a single shell for that mortar. That mortar. When I said "my" or "ours," I meant it was in our company, but that was in -- the platoon was mine, I was the platoon commander, but the company was also mine. We were all there together. So on the 8th, we didn't have a single shell.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I'm going to ask if the document under D540 can be brought back on the screen.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: It's only in English. And while we're waiting for that to come up, I'm going to ask you: There's no reference -- and we can look into this. But let me ask you this nonetheless, Mr. Tusevljak, there is no limitation on this sentence that you are only talking about one day, the 8th of June, 1992. There is no such limitation, is there? And just tell me if you remember. We can translate this document for you.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, yes, it is possible that I failed to mention that, but I -- that's what I meant. As I said, I'm not a lawyer. And when I said we didn't have any shells, I meant the 8th of June. Of course, that was on that first day. Later on, we did get shells that we used. Once we were attacked, then we would use them to fire on their lines. Not us, but the men who were in charge of that mortar.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Could we have the next page of this document on the screen for -- for the convenience of the members of the Court. So we're looking at paragraph 13.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Now --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Tusevljak, you just said that, Later on we did get shells. In fact, you said you had shells before the 8th as well, did you not?

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Do you mean before the 8th?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Yes, before the 8th of June.

utterances.speaker: SLOBODAN TUSEVLJAK [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes. We had some shells. They had them before the 8th. There were a few shells. Most of them were the incendiary, but on the 8th we didn't have any. These were just used to light up the sky at night. Those are the kind that we had.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Shin, the Chamber needs a few more minutes for other matters at this moment. We are aware that we interrupted so many times the cross-examination. We would only change our plans if you would say I'm about to finish in one or two minutes, but otherwise we'll have to continue tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: I am pretty sure I cannot finish in one or two minutes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, that's understood. Then, Witness, we expect that you'll conclude your testimony tomorrow. We had already expected it already to be concluded today but unfortunately we were able to achieve that. I again instruct you that you should not speak with anyone about your testimony, whether already given or still to be given. And we invite you to bring tomorrow or give to the Victims and Witness Section the original of this statement you said you kept after having signed it and after having sent a -- it by e-mail to the Defence. If you would by any chance still have a copy of that e-mail message, it would be appreciated if you could produce that as well. I don't know whether you still have it or not. We'd like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.30 in the morning, and you're also invited to now return, with the assistance of the usher, the bundle you received to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: A few matters. Mr. Shin, the document you identified, would that have any impact on any witness protection even if it's a name on a document or something like that? Because then we would like to inform the Victims and Witness Section about --

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: We don't -- we don't believe that it would. It's, in fact, a simply a category of documents that are treated confidentially.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then if it's not to late for the witness protection, I'll leave it to that. Another matter: P6623 has been reserved for a chart with some handwriting on it. Now, what you apparently have uploaded under 65 ter 30922 is including some metadata. Now, I don't know whether -- let me --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do understand that you did not add any metadata but that Madam Registrar did add some metadata which -- so that you're aware of that. There was no objection against admission of the -- Mr. Stojanovic, there was no objection to admission of P6623. Then P -- no, I think we reserved the number. It's now P6623 is admitted into evidence. Mr. Stojanovic, if you would carefully listen, I think Judge Fluegge has a few matters he would like to raise with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, thank you very much. We -- I would like to refer you, Mr. Stojanovic, to paragraph 2 of the statement which was prepared for this case. As I earlier indicated, in line 1 there was a reference to a paragraph 7 of the Karadzic statement. Do you agree that this should relate to paragraph 13 of the Karadzic statement which we just a minute ago had on our screens and Mr. Shin was dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would agree that it would be more practical in paragraph 13. But if you read it in the entire context, in preparation it was in paragraph 7 specifically that the witness added this story about the sniper. He says there: "On that same evening, Muslims opened fire on our houses but I had nothing to return the fire with." And then he adds that his unit was established in late May 1992 and that there was only one sniper who was a member of the battalion per establishment. But perhaps it would be more appropriate to put it in the paragraph that you have referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think in that case we can agree that it refers to paragraph 7 and paragraph 13. What about paragraph 3 of the statement in our case. I see there, the second sentence: "This is the sharpshooter I discuss in paragraphs 2 and 3 of the statement I've given in the Karadzic case." Two and 3 are not dealing with any sharpshooter, but is it correct that you refer to paragraph 26?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct, Your Honour. And I believe that in the proofing notes that I sent to you before the beginning, this correction was made and these proofing notes were also forwarded to the Prosecution as soon as I had the interview with the witness here at the Hague. And there we note that it is a correction and that it's not paragraphs 2 and 3 but rather 26.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If that is the case, which I can't confirm at the moment, you didn't deal with that during your examination-in-chief and you didn't confirm these corrections with the witness. It's not on the record up to now. If you now agree to that, then it's fine. Then it's on the record. But I don't think that this is in the proofing note we received via informal communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's possible, Your Honours. But I am pretty certain that yesterday the questions that I put to my -- to the witness I did put this question and that the witness answered with a "yes," but I can check that and I will give you the reference for it. I asked -- I put this question yesterday at the end of the work here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Stojanovic, I would like to move to another topic. Paragraph 4 of the statement which was prepared for our case here refers to the incident F4. We discussed it in detail. If I look into the indictment F4, it refers to two people who were shot and wounded by a single bullet while walking together in a certain street. Nothing about a tram. A tram appears only in F8. Perhaps this reference to F4 was taken from the Karadzic statement. I don't know the indictment in the Karadzic case. Is that really -- are we really dealing here with the incident F4, or is it something else?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are dealing with incident F4. And as for the information, the mention of "tram," that was taken out of this incident F4 and we took it out together with this sentence: From Metalka it was impossible to actually hit the tram. This sentence was deleted and this, too, was something that we forwarded to you in our proofing notes as soon as we talked with the witness, as soon as we had the interview with him. So this information, the whole bit about the tram was deleted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Why, in fact, I ask again: Why didn't you delete the entire paragraph? It makes no sense if we are not sure which incident you are referring to. In the Karadzic statement, F4 refers to an event which allegedly occurred in the Azize Sacirbegovic Street. F4 in our indictment refers to the Ivana Krndelja Street. Is that the same event or isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we stand by the position that this is the same position. We asked the witness about it. This is Ivana Krndelja Street, which by virtue of its position -- and you can see that in the document. And also from the words of the witness you can see that this was visible from the position at Ozrenska Street. So this is the incident where one bullet actually wounded two persons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. And is Azize Sacirbegovic Street nearby? Or why does the Karadzic statement refer to this street?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The street, if I'm not erring, Azize Sacirbegovic, Azize Sacirbegovic Street, if I understood that correctly, is the street that is now called Azize Sacirbegovic after the name change. The Ivana Krndelja Street that a reference was made to is the same street that is now called Azize Sacirbegovic Street. Azize Sacirbegovic Street, I believe it's the same street but it was renamed. Until the war it was called the Ivana Krndelja Street and then later it -- the name was changed and it was -- it became Azize Sacirbegovic Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to give you that reference. In our exhibit P503, 503, there is a photo document where we can see the F4 incident marked and that street is called Azize Sacirbegovic Street; however, in our case it is referred to as incident F4 on Ivana Krndelja Street.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We will adjourn for the day and will resume tomorrow, Friday, the 4th of July, at 9.30 in this same courtroom, I. But, Mr. Shin, could you tell us how much time you would still need?

utterances.speaker: MR. SHIN
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a little bit hard to estimate, but I will review and I certainly expect to finish in the first session, if that assists.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: To some extent it does. But the Chamber at this moment is not in a position to criticise you for perhaps taking more time than expected because of the pure chaos that arose. And again, Mr. Lukic, I want to express the great concern the Chamber has with the chaos, sloppiness, and whatever happens in -- at this moment in the Defence case. I leave it to that. We'll adjourn for the day and we'll resume tomorrow morning at 9.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
